title: Exact finite direct image and its stalks at rational adic coefficients
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0=\mathbf F_q,k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ containing $E$. Let $\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$, using the rationalized and common-stage coefficient categories of [def-weil-constructible-heart]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and let $f:X\to Y$ be finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the derived direct image [def-weil-derived-direct-image].

The functor $Rf_*:D^b_c(X,\Lambda)\to D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$ is $t$-exact for the standard constructible $t$-structures. Its restriction $f_*^c:\Sh_c(X,\Lambda)\to\Sh_c(Y,\Lambda)$ is exact, and for every $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ and $j\in\mathbf Z$ there are natural isomorphisms
$$\mathcal H^j(Rf_*K)\simeq f_*^c\mathcal H^j(K).$$
For a geometric point $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}k\to Y$, put $S=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}k$ and let $\mathcal F_S$ be the inverse image of $\mathcal F\in\Sh_c(X,\Lambda)$. For the finite set $P_{\bar y}=\{\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}k\to X\mid f\bar x=\bar y\}$, the restriction maps induce natural $\Lambda$-linear isomorphisms
$$(f_*^c\mathcal F)_{\bar y}\simeq H^0(S,\mathcal F_S)\simeq\bigoplus_{\bar x\in P_{\bar y}}\mathcal F_{\bar x}.$$
Here stalks, cohomology sheaves and point-fiber cohomology use [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves, def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. The isomorphisms are natural in sheaf morphisms and in isomorphisms of the finite-morphism diagram, including the semilinear isomorphisms induced by automorphisms of $k$; on the right such an isomorphism reindexes the geometric points and applies the induced stalk transports. At $\Qlb$ all these functors and maps are the scalar extensions of those at a common finite coefficient-field stage.

source.place: Tag 03QP, proposition-finite-higher-direct-image-zero (1)-(2), finite-level input; rational constructible extension using Bhatt–Scholze, The pro-etale topology for schemes, Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15. Naturality is that of the restriction/germ maps. The rational extension is a separate assertion, not the literal statement of Tag 03QP.
